title: Antigua and Barbuda Becomes First Caribbean Nation to Ban Plastic Bags
reason: Confirmed from scratch across independent sources. (1) UN in the Caribbean (caribbean.un.org, independent UN regional office) states verbatim: "In 2016 Antigua and Barbuda became the first country in Latin America and the Caribbean to ban plastic bags" — confirms country, year, and the 'first' claim. (2) The Global Plastics Policy Centre (University of Portsmouth, academic/independent) policy review confirms the ban's mechanics: tax incentives for importation of reusable bags, Chinese ("financial support from China which allowed for capacity building") funding of the public awareness campaign (logo competition co-financed by PRC + OECS Commission), the awareness slogan campaign, and the 15.1% decrease in landfill plastic within the first year. (3) Antigua's own legal order (laws.gov.ag PDF, "External Trade (Import Prohibition) Order, 2016") and multiple secondary sources corroborate the effective date "after the 30th June, 2016." (4) Caribbean News Global, an independent regional outlet, independently corroborates the landfill-proportion statistic: "The proportion of plastic at landfills declined from 19.5 percent in 2006 to 4.4 percent in 2017." One minor wrinkle: the UN SDG Partnership Platform page (sdgs.un.org) documents the rollout as a three-phase process (import ban → 6-month supermarket phase-out → end of circulation), not explicitly 'five-phased' as in the candidate description — search-engine summaries repeat a 'five-phased' characterization but I could not pin it to a primary source describing five distinct phases (it may conflate with the '5 types of plastics targeted' language used in several sources). This is a minor scope wrinkle, not a material misstatement of actor/date/country/magnitude, so I still rate the event TRUE rather than PARTIAL — every headline claim (country, year, effective date, first-in-region, tax incentives, Chinese funding, 15.1% drop, 19.5%→4.4% landfill share) is independently corroborated.
